hypotheses.reasoning: Starting at 11:07, template-svc's PutObject calls to S3 (notifications-artifacts-prod, us-east-1) came back fast with 503 ServiceUnavailable (#92, #96, #101). By #98 the aws-sdk had used up its retry quota. Because the storage write failed, template-svc returned 500 to notification-svc (#89, #117), and notification-svc passed the 500 to the gateway for POST /v1/notify (#93, #102, #112, #130). Before 11:07, request volume, redis, notif-db and notif-worker all looked normal (#74-#88), so I saw no internal traffic spike that would explain the throttling. The S3 errors were fast 503s, not hangs. Renders went back to ok from around 11:11:44 (#115), which looks like S3 recovering. The disk warning on the gateway (#30) is unrelated.

A 503 SlowDown from S3 can mean we are sending too many requests to that bucket or prefix. In that case the SDK's own retries (#98, 42 failed attempts in 60s) could make the throttling worse. I didn't see request volume go up before the errors started, so this seems less likely.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the AWS Health dashboard for S3 in us-east-1 and look at request-rate metrics for the notifications-artifacts-prod bucket. Add backoff with jitter or a circuit breaker on template-svc's S3 writes. Consider making the artifact write async or not required for /render, so an S3 problem doesn't fail the notification request. If S3 is throttling us for request rate, spread writes across more key prefixes.
